claim: The Potential Fraud Detection module renders its six pages from the national radar export: the radar with real 2024 figures, the Kentucky psychoeducation blow-up and case file, the reallocation what-if, tools and data coverage, and the backtest.
assertions: Radar: 2024 KPIs read 1,269 flagged service-years, $54.0B paid, $46.7B above the enrollment line, backtest 7/7; the first ranked row is Kentucky psychoeducation (H2027), $143.0M, 78.3% of US, suggested HIGH; the tile map shows 51 states.
Radar: at 1600px the score and suggested-tier column fits inside the table without horizontal scrolling.
Radar: filtering to Florida shows the Florida panel and 30 ranked rows.

Program blow-up: opens on Kentucky psychoeducation with the paid-vs-national chart, the "can health explain it" panel marking the rise unexplained by enrollment, and Arizona displacement (share fell from 70%).
Case file: Kentucky psychoeducation 2024 shows 7 fired and 8 pending signals, the explanation review, and the referral panel opens from "Refer to the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit".
Case file: the module grows with its content and the app footer follows it (no overlap).

Reallocation: Kentucky at 60% upheld frees $438.5M of $730.8M above the enrollment line ($314.7M federal); switching to the General Fund flags over-allocation, and "fit to available" rescales the needs to the $123.7M state share.
Tools and data coverage: 24 analyses with running, ready or needs-data status, the data sources with load dates, and the last scan console.
Backtests: all 7 known cases pass (5 flagged, 2 conventions not flagged).
